subject: Request: Temporary marketplace shelf-price carveout for AiCore enterprise bundle
messages:
From: Alex Duarte <aduarte@aicore.io>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.co>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya@aicore.io>
Date: 2027-10-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Marketplace pricing ask for AiCore enterprise bundle

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited about Redwood's latency profile and the private deployment option. We're trying to get legal/procurement across the finish line this week. Two asks from procurement: 1) a shelf-price carveout on the AWS marketplace listing for our Enterprise Bundle to match the discounted committed price in our SOW for Q4 pilot, and 2) a short-term rebate that will show on the invoice to reconcile the marketplace difference.

I've attached the SOW excerpt and a proposed invoice mockup. Can Redwood approve a temporary listing price adjustment (or an explicit rebate workflow) that lets us close the purchase via the marketplace by next Tuesday? Our AWS co-sell rep said an approved marketplace price that meets their co-sell threshold will materially improve incentives on their side.

CC'ing Priya from procurement who will send any Po approval docs.

Best,
Alex
--
Alex Duarte
Head of Cloud Partnerships
AiCore
attachments: aicore_pricing_request_20271003.pdf, marketplace_sku_bundle_sheet.xlsx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.co>
To: Alex Duarte <aduarte@aicore.io>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.co>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.co>
Date: 2027-10-03T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace pricing ask for AiCore enterprise bundle

Alex — appreciate the quick follow.

Short answer: we can consider a temporary shelf-price carveout, but it'll need Deal Desk approval and a compliance check with AWS co-sell policy. Camila, can you scope whether this fits our marketplace program constraints and if finance/legal will accept a rebate vs. direct listing change? Laura, please flag any Partner Ops implications for AWS listing updates (timeline, SKU mapping, publishing window).

Proposed immediate next step: I'll open an escalation with Deal Desk and include the SOW + invoice mockup. If Deal Desk approves a temporary listing price or an invoice-level rebate, we want a documented rollback date (end-of-pilot) and a note in the listing description to avoid future confusion.

Alex/Priya — can you confirm the absolute deadline you need this in place on the marketplace? Also include the preferred marketplace flow (1 = adjust listing price; 2 = invoice rebate that reconciles later).

Thanks,
Marcus
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

On the attachment: noted the SOW section on committed usage and the pilot term (Q4).

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.co>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.co>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.co>
Date: 2027-10-03T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace pricing ask for AiCore enterprise bundle

Looping Ben for Deal Desk — Ben, brief summary below and attachments included in Marcus's thread.

Why this is slightly out-of-band: AiCore wants the AWS marketplace unit price to match the committed SOW discount for the Q4 pilot so their procurement can route the order through the marketplace+co-sell channels. If we leave the listing at standard shelf price, AWS incentives for co-sell are materially reduced and the customer needs to commit to a separate invoice workflow that delays co-sell.

Options we think are feasible:
- Listing price adjustment (temporary): easiest for customer checkout and co-sell alignment, but requires AWS partner ops change and Marketplace publishing window (usually 48-72 hours min). Requires Partner Ops and Marketplace Product sign-off.
- Invoice-level rebate (post-invoice credit): faster from a publishing perspective (no listing change), but procurement sometimes rejects invoice credits because they want the marketplace record to reflect the committed price. This also complicates our billing and revenue recognition for the pilot.

Key constraints/asks from us to Deal Desk:
1) Approve one-time carveout to match SOW price on listing for up to 90 days (rollback date set) OR authorize a guaranteed rebate flow tied to invoice metadata.
2) Condition the approval on a signed addendum that confirms end date and that the marketplace listing will be reverted automatically.
3) Approve a waiver of the usual Marketplace minimum list-price policy for this SKU based on strategic co-sell benefit.

I've attached a draft addendum language and the SKU sheet for quick review. Marcus — noted Alex's request for deadline next Tuesday; that makes this urgent.

-Camila
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: marketplace_sku_bundle_sheet.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.co>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.co>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.co>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.co>
Date: 2027-10-05T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Marketplace pricing ask for AiCore enterprise bundle — Deal Desk intake

Thanks for the context — I pulled the SOW and the SKU sheet. Summary of Deal Desk position and required artifacts before approval:

1) We can approve a temporary listing price carveout for a period up to 60 days (shorter than requested) provided:
   - Customer signs a Marketplace Addendum (we'll use the attached template) that sets an explicit rollback date and confirms the pilot terms.
   - Finance signs off on revenue treatment (we will record at the invoiced amount; rebate handling must be described).
   - Partner Ops verifies that AWS will accept a non-standard listing price change for this SKU and completes the publishing within the required window.

2) If the above isn't acceptable to AiCore, we can alternatively approve an invoice-level rebate flow but only if Procurement confirms acceptance in writing (they must confirm invoice credits are allowed for this purchase).

3) Pricing waiver: Deal Desk will grant a one-time waiver of the minimum-list-price policy for this SKU because of strategic co-sell potential, but only for this deal id (RDW-2027-1934-AIC). Any future deals will require standard approval process.

Next steps I need from Marcus/Camila by EOD Monday:
- Signed Marketplace Addendum (or confirmation that procurement accepts invoice rebate in writing).
- Finance contact (name/email) to complete revenue treatment sign-off.
- Partner Ops (Laura) to confirm timeline for publishing if listing change chosen.

I'll hold the waiver pending those artifacts. Attaching the addendum template and a checklist.

-ben
Deal Desk 
attachments: Marketplace_Addendum_Template.docx, DealDesk_Checklist.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.co>
To: Alex Duarte <aduarte@aicore.io>, Priya Menon <priya@aicore.io>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.co>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.co>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.co>
Date: 2027-10-06T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace pricing ask for AiCore enterprise bundle

Alex/Priya — good news. Deal Desk has provisionally approved a one-time minimum-list-price waiver tied to RDW-2027-1934-AIC. We need the following by Monday EOD to finalize: 1) Signed Marketplace Addendum (Ben attached a template), 2) confirmation from your procurement that invoice credits are acceptable if we need to use the rebate path, or a confirmation that you prefer the listing-price route, and 3) billing contact for revenue sign-off.

If you can get the addendum signed and return it to ben_carter@redwood.co and copy me, we'll queue Partner Ops to publish the temporary listing price (if chosen) and push the AWS co-sell rep to prioritize the SKU.

We understand the Tuesday target — we'll do our best to meet it once the paperwork is in place.

Thanks,
Marcus
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

--- Forwarded attachments included in original thread: aicore_pricing_request_20271003.pdf, marketplace_sku_bundle_sheet.xlsx
